coaching.subject: operator-attested acceptance criteria completeness

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
vague/subjective terms present: sufficient

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact proving command for the opcert/Gerrit collateral invariant — e.g. `docker compose ps --format json | jq -e '[.[] | select(.Name=="opcert" or .Name=="gerrit")] | all(.Health == "healthy")'` — so the executor cannot accidentally pass it on a merely-running-but-unhealthy container.
evidence: 'evidenced by container health output' — no specific command given
The Testing section says 'asserted by container health rather than by inspection' but still names no command
findings.finding: The `opcert`/Gerrit collateral-invariant AC says 'evidenced by container health output' but names no specific proving command, leaving the executor to guess between `docker compose ps`, `docker inspect --format`, `docker ps --filter`, etc. One of these might not surface a failed health check.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — '`opcert` SSM fetch and Gerrit startup both still succeed after apply, evidenced by container health output'
scenarios: An executor runs `docker ps` which shows containers as 'Up' even when health checks are failing (status column only shows 'Up (unhealthy)' if the executor knows to look for it); a container could be running but its health probe failing without the executor noticing.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'evidenced by container health output' with: `docker compose ps --format json | jq -e '[.[] | select(.Name=="gerrit" or .Name=="review-bot" or .Name=="opcert")] | all(.Health == "healthy")'` returns exit 0.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the exact `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` invocation to the AC (or Testing section cross-referenced from the AC), specifying `--policy-source-arn arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role`, `--action-names bedrock:InvokeModel`, and `--resource-arns arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` (or the cross-region inference profile ARN), so the executor cannot accidentally run it as themselves.
evidence: Plan explicitly warns: 'Do NOT validate from an operator identity holding `bedrock:*`'
No complete CLI invocation is given in the AC or Testing section; the model ARN is referenced as 'the target model ARN' without pinning it
findings.finding: The `simulate-principal-policy` AC states the expected result ('returns allowed for `bedrock:InvokeModel` on the target model ARN') but does not provide the exact CLI invocation with `--policy-source-arn`, `--action-names`, and `--resource-arns` filled in. The plan already documents the importance of NOT running this as an operator with `bedrock:*`, making the exact invocation safety-critical, yet it is left implicit.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — '`aws iam simulate-principal-policy` against `rebar-gerrit-instance-role` returns allowed for `bedrock:InvokeModel` on the target model ARN'
scenarios: An executor uses their own IAM identity (which may hold `bedrock:*`) instead of `--policy-source-arn` for the instance role, or forgets `--resource-arns`, and gets a false-positive 'allowed' that masks a misconfiguration.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact filename for the new runbook (e.g. `infra/runbooks/bedrock-grant-verification.md`) so the AC can be proven with a concrete `ls`/`cat` command rather than a directory scan.
evidence: 'infra/runbooks/' — directory only, no filename
The AC has no proving command (e.g. `ls infra/runbooks/bedrock-grant.md`) that would make it evaluable in-session
findings.finding: The runbook deliverable is listed in Scope ('`infra/runbooks/` — the verification commands from AC1/AC2 recorded as a runbook check') and in the AC ('`infra/runbooks/` carries the verification recipe'), but no filename is specified. A future operator, or a reviewer checking the AC, cannot deterministically verify the runbook exists without knowing the file to `git show` or `cat`.
findings.location: Scope bullet — 'infra/runbooks/ — the verification commands from AC1/AC2 recorded as a runbook check'; Acceptance Criteria — 'infra/runbooks/ carries the verification recipe this story used'
scenarios: An executor creates `infra/runbooks/s7-notes.txt`; a reviewer looks for `infra/runbooks/bedrock-iam-verification.md`; neither can verify the other's check.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the file `infra/runbooks/bedrock-grant-verification.md` and update the AC proving command to `cat infra/runbooks/bedrock-grant-verification.md` (exits 0 if present, fails if absent).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the Scope description of the runbook with its AC: replace 'the verification commands from AC1/AC2' with 'the simulate-principal-policy invocation and the from-instance (SSM) Converse check' (or expand to list all intended commands explicitly) so both sections name the same content.
evidence: Scope: 'infra/runbooks/ — the verification commands from AC1/AC2 recorded as a runbook check'

Runbook AC: 'infra/runbooks/ carries the verification recipe this story used — the simulate-principal-policy invocation and the from-instance Converse check — so a future operator can re-verify the grant without rediscovering that a wildcard-holding identity cannot validate it'
AC1 is defined as 'an IMDSv2 token request from inside the review-bot container' — not simulate-principal-policy
AC2 (inferred) is 'aws sts get-caller-identity' — not the from-instance Converse check
findings.finding: The Scope section describes the runbook deliverable as carrying 'the verification commands from AC1/AC2', but the runbook's own AC specifies it must contain the `simulate-principal-policy` invocation and the from-instance (SSM) Converse check. AC1 is the IMDS token probe; AC2 is `sts get-caller-identity` — neither is what the runbook AC requires. An implementer reading Scope to understand what to write in the runbook will produce the wrong content.
findings.location: Scope section ('infra/runbooks/ — the verification commands from AC1/AC2 recorded as a runbook check') vs runbook AC ('the simulate-principal-policy invocation and the from-instance Converse check')
scenarios: Executor reads Scope, writes a runbook with AC1 IMDS probe and sts get-caller-identity commands, marks the criterion done — runbook is missing the two checks the AC actually specifies, leaving a future operator without the critical from-instance validation recipe.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, change 'the verification commands from AC1/AC2 recorded as a runbook check' to 'the simulate-principal-policy invocation (AC: simulate-principal-policy check) and the from-instance SSM Converse call (AC: from-instance Converse check), recorded so a future operator can re-verify the grant without a wildcard-holding identity masking the result'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` check and the from-instance SSM Converse call to the Testing section's structured list so it matches the three-layer verification the Approach declares mandatory and the AC enforces.
evidence: Approach: 'How this must be verified — three layers, and the third is not optional. (1) simulate-principal-policy against the role… (2) a real Converse call FROM the instance… (3) a negative control'

Testing section lists: precondition probe (AC1), happy path (from-container only), least-privilege oracle (non-Claude), collateral invariant, terraform plan — no simulate-principal-policy, no from-instance SSM call

AC: 'a real bedrock-runtime converse call executed FROM the instance (SSM, as the instance role) returns a model response — the ONLY check that reveals which IAM action the service authorizes against'
AC: 'aws iam simulate-principal-policy against rebar-gerrit-instance-role returns allowed for bedrock:InvokeModel'
findings.finding: The Testing section's structured list of checks omits two verifications that the Approach marks mandatory ('not optional') and the AC makes explicit pass/fail criteria: (1) `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` against the role, and (2) the from-instance SSM Converse call. An executor following only the Testing section as the authoritative test plan would skip both checks, directly contradicting the Approach's explicit statement that the third layer (from-instance call) 'is not optional'.
findings.location: Testing section (structured list) vs Approach section ('How this must be verified — three layers, and the third is not optional') vs AC items for simulate-principal-policy and from-instance Converse
scenarios: Executor treats Testing section as the authoritative checklist, runs all listed tests, declares done — the from-instance SSM call (the only real authorization proof) and simulate-principal-policy were never run, but no test in the Testing section flagged the omission.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Testing section, add two bullet points after the happy-path entry: '- from-instance authorization proof: via SSM AWS-RunShellScript on the instance (as rebar-gerrit-instance-role), run a bedrock-runtime Converse call to a Claude model — the only check that reveals which IAM action the service authorizes against (mirrors the call that caught the original wrong grant)' and '- policy-language check: `aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn <role-arn> --action-names bedrock:InvokeModel --resource-arns <claude-model-arn>` returns ALLOW — necessary but not sufficient on its own'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback statement for the hop-limit contingency path — e.g., 'to revert: set `http_put_response_hop_limit = 1` in `metadata_options`, run `terraform apply`, and confirm via `aws ec2 describe-instances` that the value is restored; no instance stop/start required because `ModifyInstanceMetadataOptions` is in-place' — so the back-out procedure is self-contained alongside the justification.
evidence: 'if AC1 shows IMDS is NOT reachable from the review-bot container, set `http_put_response_hop_limit = 2` in `metadata_options`'
'The exposure that raises is bounded and stated plainly'
No statement anywhere of how to revert the hop-limit change if it causes a problem post-apply

T4 criterion: 'The REMEDY for a destructive/breaking change is an explicit rollback/back-out plan or expand-contract sequencing — checking only that breakage is acknowledged is insufficient; require the reversibility mechanism'
findings.finding: The contingency path (raising `http_put_response_hop_limit` to 2) changes existing EC2 instance metadata behavior and is explicitly justified, but the plan provides no rollback/back-out procedure if that change causes unexpected issues after apply.
findings.location: Approach section — contingency paragraph; Scope — `infra/terraform/main.tf`; final AC line (HttpPutResponseHopLimit check)
scenarios: Hop-limit increase is applied under the contingency; an unanticipated container (e.g. a future workload added to the compose file) gains IMDS access; operator wants to revert but has no documented procedure.
Post-apply, opcert or Gerrit behaves unexpectedly due to changed IMDS routing; without a rollback recipe the operator must rediscover that reverting to hop_limit=1 via terraform is the fix.
findings.suggested_fix: In the contingency paragraph (or as an additional bullet under the final AC), add: 'Rollback: revert `http_put_response_hop_limit` to `1` in `main.tf`, run `terraform apply`; AWS applies the change in-place via `ModifyInstanceMetadataOptions` with no instance restart. Confirm with `aws ec2 describe-instances --query Reservations[].Instances[].MetadataOptions`.`

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the `infra/runbooks/` entry (or add a brief ADR / AGENTS.md note) to capture the durable architectural decision: the Converse API authorizes against `bedrock:InvokeModel`, the simulator cannot distinguish these, and `bedrock:Converse` must not be granted — so future maintainers don't re-derive this from scratch.
evidence: 'infra/runbooks/ — the verification commands from AC1/AC2 recorded as a runbook check' — scoped to commands only, not the decision rationale
'This story briefly granted bedrock:Converse + bedrock:ConverseStream. That was wrong and is corrected here' — this institutional knowledge lives only in the plan/story text
ADR 0046 is conditioned on the hop-limit contingency firing; no ADR is unconditionally created for the InvokeModel/Converse action-name contract
ABSENCE: no AC or scope item calls for recording the InvokeModel-vs-Converse authorization contract in a durable artifact (ADR, AGENTS.md, or runbook prose section)
findings.finding: The architectural decision that `bedrock:InvokeModel` (not `bedrock:Converse`) is the IAM action the Converse API authorizes against is documented only in ephemeral story/plan text. The runbook AC (`infra/runbooks/`) is scoped to 'the verification recipe... the simulate-principal-policy invocation and the from-instance Converse check' — it does not capture the decision rationale. A future maintainer editing `iam_s7.tf` (e.g., to extend permissions or audit the grant) will not find a durable artifact explaining why `bedrock:Converse` must NOT be granted and why the simulator cannot be trusted as sole evidence.
findings.location: Scope section / AC (infra/runbooks/ criterion) / Approach section 'The action name is bedrock:InvokeModel'
scenarios: A future story extends the Bedrock grant (e.g., adds a new model family) and an engineer consults `iam_s7.tf` + the runbook, finds only CLI commands, re-runs simulate-custom-policy for `bedrock:Converse`, sees `implicitDeny`, and re-introduces the wrong action — the exact failure mode the plan warns against.

An audit of IAM policy files surfaces `bedrock:InvokeModel` without explanation; an auditor flags it as likely wrong (should be `bedrock:Converse`) and raises a finding, requiring re-discovery of the same evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a prose 'Decision rationale' section to the new runbook file (alongside the CLI commands) stating: (1) Bedrock Converse API checks `bedrock:InvokeModel` at authorization time, not `bedrock:Converse`; (2) `aws iam simulate-custom-policy` reports the named action's policy result, not the service's actual authorization check — only a real call reveals this; (3) `bedrock:Converse` is deliberately absent from the grant. Alternatively, add a one-paragraph entry to `docs/adr/0046-security-posture-and-accepted-limitations.md` unconditionally (not gated on the hop-limit contingency).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (or extend an existing operator-attested AC) requiring that `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` be confirmed as the action actually checked by ConverseStream — either by a remove-and-retest step run in-session before this story closes, or by an explicit out-of-band AWS documentation citation — so the least-privilege claim for the streaming action is grounded in this story rather than deferred to S8.
evidence: iam_s7.tf lines 54-56: 'SCOPE OF THAT PROOF: it shows the streaming path SUCCEEDS under this policy. It does NOT by itself identify which IAM action ConverseStream authorizes against, since the policy grants both actions at once; only removing one and re-testing would show that, which is the deny-side control S8's fault injection performs.'

Plan body: 'bedrock:InvokeModel + bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream (NOT the Converse pair)' — the story's own evidentiary standard (runtime proof of which action the service checks, not just that a call succeeds) is applied to InvokeModel but structurally cannot be applied to InvokeModelWithResponseStream within this story's final deployed state.
ABSENCE: no AC requires confirming that revoking bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream causes ConverseStream calls to fail, so the action's necessity is unverifiable without S8 landing.

Pattern evidence: the Converse API authorizes against bedrock:InvokeModel rather than bedrock:Converse — the same 'API name ≠ IAM action name' pattern makes it plausible that ConverseStream also authorizes against bedrock:InvokeModel, which would make the second action dead blast radius.
findings.finding: bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream is granted and its streaming success is verified, but which IAM action the ConverseStream API actually authorizes against cannot be determined from the combined-policy success proof alone. The plan explicitly defers the deny-side disambiguation to S8 fault injection, but that means this story ships with an unverified least-privilege claim: if bedrock:InvokeModel alone is sufficient for ConverseStream (consistent with Bedrock's pattern where InvokeModel is the general authorization action), the second action is unnecessary blast radius that contradicts the story's own stated least-privilege goal — and no AC within this story closes the loop.
findings.location: Approach section — 'bedrock:InvokeModel + bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream … NOT the Converse pair'; iam_s7.tf:44-56; no covering AC
scenarios: If bedrock:InvokeModel is sufficient for both Converse and ConverseStream, then bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream is an unnecessary grant — widening blast radius with no functional benefit, which directly contradicts the story's stated least-privilege goal.

If S8 never ships or defers the fault injection, this disambiguation is never closed, and the grant permanently carries an unverified action that future operators cannot distinguish as load-bearing or vestigial from any artifact in this story.
findings.suggested_fix: The lowest-cost resolution is a targeted AWS IAM documentation cite: if AWS publishes that ConverseStream authorizes against bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream (distinct from InvokeModel), add the citation to the iam_s7.tf comment and the runbook. If documentation is ambiguous, run the remove-and-retest step in-session: temporarily remove bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream from a test policy copy attached to the role, call converse_stream, and record whether the result is allowed or AccessDeniedException. This is the same evidence standard the plan already applied to InvokeModel and takes under five minutes via SSM.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (or expand the streaming AC) requiring a deny-side test: temporarily remove `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` from the policy and confirm whether a `converse_stream` call fails with `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` denied — this is the only evidence that settles whether the action is load-bearing vs. redundant, per the plan's own evidentiary standard for action names.
evidence: iam_s7.tf:54-56: 'SCOPE OF THAT PROOF: it shows the streaming path SUCCEEDS under this policy. It does NOT by itself identify which IAM action ConverseStream authorizes against, since the policy grants both actions; the deny-side control for that is S8's fault injection.'
Plan Approach section: 'So the grant is bedrock:InvokeModel + bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream' — stated as fact, not as a pending verification.

The plan's own lesson: 'the policy simulator answers what does the policy language permit for the action you NAMED, never which action the service CHECKS. Only a real call distinguishes those two questions.' — the same gap applies to InvokeModelWithResponseStream.
ABSENCE: no AC line requires a deny-test (remove InvokeModelWithResponseStream, retry streaming call) before this story closes.
findings.finding: `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` is asserted as the correct/required IAM action for the ConverseStream API path, but by the plan's own evidentiary standard this is unverified: the streaming call succeeded with BOTH InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream granted simultaneously, so there is no deny-side proof that InvokeModelWithResponseStream is load-bearing rather than redundant. The plan explicitly notes this gap and defers the deny-side control to 'S8's fault injection' — but S8 is a downstream story, leaving the current story shipping an unresolved capability assertion about an IAM action name, which is exactly the class of error that produced the wrong bedrock:Converse grant in the first pass.
findings.location: iam_s7.tf lines 44-56 / Approach section 'InvokeModelWithResponseStream is EXERCISED, not assumed'
scenarios: If InvokeModel alone authorizes ConverseStream (as it does for Converse), then InvokeModelWithResponseStream is a redundant grant that widens blast radius for no benefit — the plan would have repeated the same mistake it documented avoiding.
S8 fault injection deferred to a future story means this story closes with an unresolved IAM action assertion that the plan's own standard requires empirical proof for.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Acceptance Criteria: 'A real `converse_stream` call with ONLY `bedrock:InvokeModel` granted (temporarily remove `InvokeModelWithResponseStream`) returns either success (proving InvokeModel alone authorizes streaming, making InvokeModelWithResponseStream redundant) or AccessDeniedException naming `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` (proving it is required). Record the outcome and update the grant accordingly.' This can be done in-session via a temporary policy edit + retest, before this story closes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (or expand the contingency AC) requiring the operator to run `terraform plan` and confirm the metadata_options change shows as an **in-place update** (no `forces replacement`) before applying the hop-limit contingency.
evidence: Plan says: 'set http_put_response_hop_limit = 2 in metadata_options, keeping http_tokens = required'
main.tf:50-54 shows the existing metadata_options block with no http_put_response_hop_limit set
No AC or Scope line says 'verify terraform plan shows no replace/destroy before applying the contingency'

The data volume uses prevent_destroy but the instance itself does not; an instance replacement would detach the EBS volume, disassociate the EIP briefly, and require manual re-attachment — a non-trivial blast radius on the production Gerrit host
findings.finding: The hop-limit contingency path modifies `metadata_options` on the live `aws_instance.gerrit` resource, but the plan never instructs the operator to inspect the terraform plan output for a ForceNew (instance replacement) before applying — and never confirms that changing `http_put_response_hop_limit` is an in-place update rather than a replacement in the AWS provider version in use.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Contingency, decided in advance'; Scope section — 'infra/terraform/main.tf — metadata_options (:50-54), touched ONLY under the AC1 contingency'; AC (contingency AC)
scenarios: Operator hits the contingency path, edits main.tf to add http_put_response_hop_limit=2, and applies without checking the plan; if the provider marks metadata_options as ForceNew in any configuration, the instance is replaced, detaching the data volume and disrupting Gerrit
A future provider upgrade changes the ForceNew behavior; without a plan-review gate in the AC, the risk is silently elevated
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the contingency AC: 'Before applying, run `terraform plan -out contingency.tfplan` and confirm the aws_instance.gerrit change is shown as `~ update` (in-place), NOT `- must be replaced`. Do not apply if plan shows a replacement.' The AWS provider (≥5.0) does support metadata_options as an in-place change, but this must be verified in the plan output before applying on the live host.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit hard dependency or AC noting that S8's deny-side fault injection (removing `InvokeModelWithResponseStream` and confirming ConverseStream then fails) is required to complete the IAM-action verification for streaming, and that until S8 closes this, the `InvokeModelWithResponseStream` grant is provisional over-grant.
evidence: Plan quote: 'It does NOT by itself identify which IAM action ConverseStream authorizes against, since the policy grants both actions; the deny-side control for that is S8's fault injection.'
iam_s7.tf comment: 'SCOPE OF THAT PROOF: it shows the streaming path SUCCEEDS under this policy. It does NOT by itself identify which IAM action ConverseStream authorizes against'
The plan commits the `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` grant in shipped Terraform (iam_s7.tf:62) on the basis of a success-only test, with IAM-action identity deferred to S8
Evidence class: Partially-verified — the integration surface exists and the call succeeds, but the specific IAM action name ConverseStream authorizes against is unconfirmed by a deny-side test
findings.finding: `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` is asserted as the correct IAM action for the ConverseStream API but is not empirically proven: the plan explicitly concedes it 'does NOT identify which IAM action ConverseStream authorizes against' because the policy grants both InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream simultaneously. Unlike InvokeModel (proven by runtime AccessDeniedException), no deny-side runtime test isolates which action ConverseStream checks.
findings.location: Approach section — 'InvokeModelWithResponseStream is EXERCISED, not assumed'; iam_s7.tf:44-56; runbooks/bedrock-access.md:105-108
scenarios: If ConverseStream actually authorizes against `bedrock:InvokeModel` (same as Converse), then `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` is over-granted blast radius that goes undetected until S8's fault injection.
If S8 is deprioritized or descoped, the unverified grant persists indefinitely.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the contingency section (hop_limit=2 path), explicitly acknowledge that the internet-facing Gerrit container (ports 443/29418 open to 0.0.0.0/0) also gains IMDS/Bedrock access, state why the scoped Claude-only grant bounds the blast radius acceptably, and record this in ADR 0046 alongside the existing bounded-exposure rationale.
evidence: 'all three are first-party rebar components that already receive instance-role-derived secrets through the .env that fetch-secrets.sh writes. Raising the hop limit therefore widens reach to containers that are already inside the same trust boundary'
network.tf:28-55: Gerrit SG opens 443/0.0.0.0/0 and 29418/0.0.0.0/0 inbound — Gerrit container is directly internet-reachable, unlike review-bot (127.0.0.1 loopback only)
docker-compose.yml:38: Gerrit publishes '127.0.0.1:8080:8080' for nginx proxy BUT also '29418:29418' directly
ABSENCE: contingency blast-radius rationale does not distinguish between the internet-facing Gerrit container and the loopback-only review-bot when asserting 'same trust boundary'
findings.finding: Under the hop-limit contingency (http_put_response_hop_limit = 2), the Gerrit container — which is directly internet-reachable on ports 443 and 29418 — gains the ability to obtain instance-role credentials including the new `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant via IMDS. The plan's bounded-exposure rationale treats all three containers as equivalent members of the same trust boundary, but the Gerrit container is the only one with direct internet ingress, making it a meaningfully higher-exposure surface under a container-compromise scenario. The contingency section does not differentiate this vector or state the accepted posture for the Gerrit container specifically.
findings.location: Plan section 'Approach' — contingency paragraph; 'Explicitly NOT doing iptables containment'
scenarios: External attacker exploits a Gerrit vulnerability via port 29418 or 443 to obtain RCE in the Gerrit container; under hop_limit=2, the Gerrit container can call IMDS, assume the instance role, and invoke `bedrock:InvokeModel` (e.g., for data exfiltration or cost abuse). The plan's iptables-not-applicable reasoning forecloses the mitigation, but the residual risk for this specific vector is not stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the contingency paragraph and to the ADR 0046 entry: 'The Gerrit container (ports 443 and 29418 internet-facing) is included in this widening; residual risk is bounded to Claude-model invocation only (no data-store or admin actions in the grant) and is accepted at this assurance level.'

findings.finding: The AC `grep -rn 'bedrock:Converse' infra/terraform/` will produce non-empty output and therefore appear to FAIL, because iam_s7.tf contains the literal string 'bedrock:Converse' in comment lines (lines 14 and 18 of iam_s7.tf explain why that action name is NOT granted). The AC is semantically correct in intent — verify the action isn't granted — but the grep test as written cannot distinguish a comment from a grant.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the AC with: "`grep -rn '"bedrock:Converse"' infra/terraform/` is empty` (double-quoted string match targets only HCL string literals, not comment prose), or use `grep -v '#'` to strip comment lines before checking.

findings.finding: AC8's grep command (`grep -rn 'bedrock:Converse' infra/terraform/`) will produce non-empty output on the already-committed `iam_s7.tf`, because that file contains the string 'bedrock:Converse' in two comment lines (lines 14 and 18) explaining why the wrong action must NOT be granted. The AC will therefore falsely fail — not because Converse is granted, but because the grep matches comments.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC8: `grep -rn 'bedrock:Converse' infra/terraform/` is empty
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the AC line with: `- [ ] \`grep -rn 'bedrock:Converse' infra/terraform/ | grep -v '^[^:]*:#'\` is empty — Converse must not appear as a granted action (comment-only occurrences are expected and intentional)

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)
